title: A cache simulator: ways, and what to throw away

prereqs.why: The whole of `decode` is this: which bits are the offset, which are the index, and what is left.
Each field is one shift and one mask, and the mask for a zero-width field is the case that catches people.
Three files are compiled separately and linked, so a signature that does not match its declaration is a link error rather than a compile error.
A set with several ways is the whole of this milestone, and the replacement policy is the choice it forces.

statement:
**Milestone 2 of 3.** The same simulator, now with more than one line
per set — and therefore, for the first time, a choice about what to
throw away.

### What is new

`main.cpp` now reads **three** numbers: `<sets> <ways> <blockBytes>`.
A set holds `ways` lines, searched in parallel by a real cache and in a
loop by this one. `stats` grows a third number.

```
decode <addr>   print  tag=<t> index=<i> offset=<o>
read <addr>     print  hit  or  miss
stats           print  <hits> hits, <misses> misses, <evictions> evictions
```

The header gains one method:

```cpp
std::size_t evictions() const;
```

### The rules, exactly

- A **hit** is a line in this set that is valid and whose tag matches.
- On a **miss**, the block is brought in. If any way of the set has
  never been used, it goes there and **nothing is evicted** — filling an
  empty way is not an eviction, and the counter must not move.
- If every way is in use, the line **least recently used** is thrown
  out, and that is one eviction. "Used" means a hit on it or the access
  that brought it in.
- Least recently *used*, not first in. The difference is testable and it
  is tested: read A, B, A, C with two ways evicts **B**, so A is still
  there afterwards. A queue would have thrown out A.
- `decode` is unchanged. Associativity does not touch the address.

### The sample

```
1 2 16                   one set of two sixteen-byte lines
read 0            ->     miss      way 0, nothing evicted
read 100          ->     miss      way 1, nothing evicted
read 0            ->     hit       and 0 is now the recent one
read 200          ->     miss      both ways busy: 100 is the old one
read 0            ->     hit       so 0 survived
read 100          ->     miss      100 did not
stats             ->     2 hits, 4 misses, 2 evictions
```

### Carrying your work forward

Your `include/cache.hpp` and `src/cache.cpp` come with you from
milestone 1. Two things follow from that:

- If you left a file untouched in milestone 1, you get **this**
  milestone's version of it, which is the one that declares
  `evictions()`.
- If you edited the header in milestone 1, you keep **your** version —
  and yours does not declare `evictions()`, so `main.cpp` will not link
  until you add it. The compiler will say so by name.

Nothing of yours is ever replaced silently. Milestone 1 keeps its own
drafts and its own submissions.
hints: The lines of set `i` are `lines_[i * ways_]` through `lines_[i * ways_ + ways_ - 1]`. Everything in `access` is a loop over that range.
Three passes, and in this order: look for a matching valid line; if there is none, look for an invalid one; only if there is none of those do you pick a victim and count an eviction.

`stamp` is there for the policy. Keep a counter on the cache, increment it on every access, and write it into the line you just touched — on a hit as well as on a fill. The victim is the line with the smallest stamp.

Updating `stamp` only when a line is filled gives you first-in-first-out, not least-recently-used, and the test with `read 0 / read 200 / read 0 / read 400 / read 0` is the one that tells the two apart.
